answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can hold payment in escrow until an independent verifier confirms the work, and charge a small non-refundable fee for each new identity. Like a ripple from one stone, a fake agent can only spawn copies by paying again for each, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand fees. Like yarrow spreading slowly, trust grows only through verified work: a wharf checks every ship's manifest before docking, so new agents start with tiny escrow limits that grow only after verified deliveries, making fake identities pay full price to earn almost nothing.
